content.thinking:
Interesting — the flag provider shows no recent changes, but logs indicate the evaluation ratio flipped, and no mitigation was ever attempted, just an escalation with a draft PR while the service stayed down. Piecing it together, I believe the monthly-spend-feature flag flipped active at 15:45, triggering a divide-by-zero in spend_summary.py:47, though I'm inferring this from the logs rather than confirmed data.

I need to keep several assumptions in mind: the flag attribution rests only on evaluation counts, there's no deploy or config change on record, the outage is presumed ongoing since the last check, and the affected area is the account page with unverified impact figures as lower bounds.

For the summary, I'll frame this generically as customers seeing errors on the account page, with roughly a third of requests failing starting 15:45 UTC and continuing at least through 15:51 — an automated responder investigated, made no live changes, and opened a draft fix for human review. I want to attribute the error rate figures directly to the monitoring data rather than presenting them as something I calculated myself, so I'll phrase it as reported by the alerting metrics.

assumptions: The cause is inferred, not confirmed: the flag provider's history showed zero recent flag changes, so the claim that `monthly-spend-feature` was switched on rests entirely on the service's own per-minute evaluation log lines changing from 'off' to 'on' at 15:45-15:46.

That the flag flip caused the errors rather than merely coinciding with them is inferred from timing plus the change in error signature (ClientDisconnected before 15:45, ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 from 15:45 on). No hypothesis was ever tested by acting on it, so nothing was confirmed by rollback or by any other intervention.

The absence of a deploy or config change is taken from change-event queries over windows of 51, 111 and 1491 minutes; a change outside those windows or one not recorded as a production change event would not have been seen.

The incident is assumed to have continued past the end of the metrics window. All duration and impact figures quoted are lower bounds read off that truncated window, not measurements of the full event.
Impact is assumed to be confined to the account page, because that is the only surface named in the error logs; no other endpoint or service was checked.
No customer-facing effect beyond failed account page loads (e.g. checkout, orders, data corruption) was assessed either way.
The draft pull request is an untested proposal. It was not reviewed, merged or deployed within the incident, and there is no evidence in the record that it resolves the fault.

The throughput figure of 200 evaluations per minute appears constant across every log minute; whether that is real traffic or a fixed synthetic rate was not established, so the absolute count of affected shoppers cannot be derived from it.
input.executive_summary:
Starting 15:45 UTC on 27 September 2026, shoppers loading their account page on the online store began getting errors. Per the service's monitoring, the failure rate went from around 1% of requests before the onset to roughly 31% on average (peaking near 36.5%) — so a large minority of shoppers trying to view their account were affected, while the rest of the store continued to work. The service had still not recovered as of the last minute of data available, so the fault lasted at least from 15:45 to the end of that window; the true duration and the true number of affected shoppers are not known and are larger than any figure quoted here.

The automated responder picked up the alert about six minutes after the onset, pulled metrics, logs and change records three times over, and each time settled on the same single explanation — a newly-activated feature being switched on for the account page. It could not find a safe automated action to take: no mitigation was proposed and no change was made to production, so nothing was rolled back, disabled or restarted. Roughly two minutes after taking the incident, it drafted a proposed code fix as a pull request and escalated the incident to humans. At the point the record ends, the fault was still live and awaiting a human to either turn the new feature off or review and ship the proposed fix.
input.root_cause: At 15:45 UTC the `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop began evaluating "on" (142 off / 58 on in that minute, fully on by 15:46), activating a code path that raises `ZeroDivisionError` at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 whenever it computes a monthly spend summary, so account page requests that hit the new path failed. Note the attribution is circumstantial: the flag provider's change history reported no recent flag changes and no deploy or config change was recorded in the preceding day, so the flip is inferred from the per-minute evaluation counts in the service's own logs rather than from a recorded change event.
